summary:
Lunar Frontier – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive educational simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It allows students to experience the challenges of managing a lunar or Martian outpost by making decisions that affect crew survival and mission success.

The platform features an interactive mission dashboard where users can customize missions, select crew sizes, choose landing profiles, and manage essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, energy, radiation protection, and crew health. It also includes a research lab, infrastructure upgrades, random mission events, objectives, and a mission log to track decisions and progress.

Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a single self-contained web application, the project incorporates resource-management calculations, interactive elements, and browser-based save/load functionality. Its educational approach draws inspiration from NASA concepts such as the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS), and the Veggie space farming system.

The main objective is to make space exploration more accessible and engaging by teaching students about resource management, sustainability, critical thinking, and the complexities of establishing human settlements beyond Earth.
details:
Lunar Frontier – Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Lunar Frontier is an interactive space exploration simulator that I developed to give students an idea of what it would actually be like to manage a human settlement on the Moon or Mars.

The idea is simple: instead of just reading about space exploration, users get to experience some of its challenges themselves. They can create their own missions, choose crew sizes and landing profiles, and manage important resources such as oxygen, water, food, energy, and crew health. The simulator also includes random mission events, research opportunities, infrastructure upgrades, objectives, and a mission log. Every decision matters because poor resource management or unexpected events can affect the success of the mission.

The main benefit of the project is that it combines learning with practical decision-making. It helps students develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills while introducing them to some of the real challenges astronauts and engineers face during space missions. My goal is to make space science more interesting and accessible, especially for students who are interested in STEM.

I developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code as my main development environment. HTML was used to structure the website, CSS for the design and layout, and JavaScript to handle the interactive features, calculations, and mission systems. I also used Netlify to host the project online.

What makes Lunar Frontier creative is that it turns a complex scientific topic into something users can actually interact with. Rather than simply explaining how a lunar settlement works, it lets users make decisions and see how those decisions affect their mission.

Throughout development, I focused on balancing scientific accuracy with simplicity and usability. I wanted the simulation to be challenging enough to be interesting without making it too complicated for students. I also took inspiration from real NASA technologies and concepts, particularly life-support systems and space agriculture.
